IPT.evidence_source: [/page/6/Text/6] The findings of this study indicate that either cognitive-behavioural therapy or a brief 'supportive' therapy may be effective for child and adolescent depression in the short term, as both the structured cognitive-behavioural therapy and the supportive non-focused intervention had a positive post-treatment effect on depressive and anxiety symptoms, self-esteem and social functioning. [/page/7/Text/4] As in previous programmes for youngsters and adults (Powell & Oei, 1991), the cognitive-behavioural treatment included a combination of techniques such as self-monitoring, self-control, social problem-solving and cognitive restructuring rather than 'pure' cognitive techniques.

[/page/6/Text/7] Severity of psychiatric symptoms at the first assessment (child- or parent-reported) also predicted post-treatment outcome.
